extracted.intended_audience: speculative fiction writers submitting to Clarkesworld Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting short speculative fiction (science fiction, fantasy, and related work) to Clarkesworld Magazine, including length, content preferences, disallowed tropes, and strict submission policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be between 1,000 and 22,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Range is explicit: minimum 1,000 words, maximum 22,000 words. Submit only works within this span.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarkesworld pays above SFWA professional rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information for authors about compensation: submissions meeting acceptance will be paid higher than SFWA pro rates (no specific per-word figure given on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre: Science fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepts science fiction; need not be 'hard' SF, but rigor is appreciated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SF stories are welcome across the spectrum; authors should aim for internal rigor or believable logical/technical consistency even if not 'hard' SF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre: Fantasy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepts fantasy—can be folkloric, contemporary, surreal, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide interpretation of fantasy allowed; authors may use folkloric, modern, or surreal approaches so long as the work fits the magazine's speculative remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre: Broad speculative fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcomes speculative fiction broadly across the spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not limited to narrowly-defined subgenres; submissions that are speculative in concept or tone are within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: predictable 'Earth' reveal (Tirran/Tellus trope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit stories where a planet is named Tirran or Tellus and turns out to be Earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among Neil Clarke's 'Things I Will Not Buy' — this specific cliché is explicitly unwelcome as an overused twist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: cute alien turns out evil
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stories where the cute alien later turns out to be evil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This trope is called out as a tired reversal; such twists that rely on trope bait-and-switch are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: preachy genre superiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stories with deep messages about how SF/fantasy is better than mundane fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write metafictional indictments asserting speculative fiction's superiority; avoid didactic pieces that argue genre primacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: protagonist suffering for suffering's sake
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stories where the protagonist's hardships exist only for the protagonist to bear them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes meaningful stakes and purpose: hardships should serve story, character development, or theme, not gratuitous suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: non-twists or fake twists
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid twist endings that don't actually twist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twists should be earned, surprising, and meaningful; avoid predictable or hollow 'twists' that add no real change to story interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: stories featuring serial killers
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories featuring serial killers are generally not wanted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serial-killer-centered narratives are flagged as undesirable on the editor's exclusion list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: most stories about writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Most stories about writers are not wanted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-stories focusing on writers as a commonplace subject are usually rejected; such setups are on the 'will not buy' list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: technological lecturing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stories where the entire plot is technological lecturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let plot devolve into long expository or didactic tech explanation; story should remain character-driven and engaging rather than a lecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: lengthy dream sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Lengthy dream sequences are discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extended dream content that substitutes for plot or character work is unwelcome; use dreams sparingly and purposefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: mimicry without originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid deliberately mimicking an established style without bringing anything new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imitation that lacks fresh perspective or original contribution is unacceptable; nods or homage must still offer novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: No AI-assisted work
rubrics_metrics.description: No AI-assisted work whatsoever is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy is strict: submitting AI-assisted stories 'may result in being banned from submitting.' Authors must ensure no AI assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous submissions are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only to Clarkesworld while the piece is under consideration; do not send the same story elsewhere simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-rejection cooling period
rubrics_metrics.description: 7-day cooling period after rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must wait seven days after a rejection before resubmitting (applies to the same work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should have a strong opening; Clarkesworld is known for tightly-edited, sharp openers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with compelling lines/scenes; immediate engagement and tightly-edited openings are a hallmark of accepted pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising ideas with emotional grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction should combine surprising ideas with emotional grounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovative concepts should be paired with genuine emotional stakes; ingenuity alone is not enough without emotional resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fresh angle on SF tropes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a fresh angle on familiar SF tropes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors value original spins on established concepts rather than rehashing clichés; novelty in treatment is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse perspectives and global settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions from diverse perspectives and global settings are welcomed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarkesworld encourages varied cultural viewpoints and international settings; diversity of voice and setting is seen as a positive quality hallmark.
